meta.scope: Phase 2b increment 3 - the CV OR workpiece itself (the part that travels the Hot Zone): bell / outer race, stem, spline end, base flange, part marks and the L5 heat visualisation. It is modelled once, mounted in the Phase 2a induction fixture; further part instances along the line, the AutoID reader station, laser marking station, unload/boxing station and the inspection modes stay in later increments. GAGE remains DEFERRED (NV-016).
meta.note: Statuses are self-assessed against PHOTO-05 (induction bowl station close-up, part on the fixture under coolant - contact-sheet review only, medium confidence), PHOTO-09 (induction station, stem quench, part wet - contact-sheet review only), PHOTO-12 (oven exit tray of parts) and Project_Document.pdf pages 3 and 5 (EQ-005/EQ-006 laser marking and 2D code, EQ-007 spline gages, QN-002 part seating, QN-004 bell colour, QN-005 stem heat zone, GD-004 OPD marking, GS-004 'V' mark, PR-001/PR-002 Z2 axis positions). No dimensioned drawing or CAD exists (NV-011) and NO reference photograph shows the workpiece in isolation (NV-018), so every dimension is ESTIMATED from photo proportions or ASSUMED for features that are never visible; nothing is MEASURED. Materials are named only as 'part steel': no grade is stated in any source. The spline tooth count, bolt-hole pattern, cage seat and mark positions are invented placements of documented features, flagged ASSUMED. L5 heat glow and the coolant film are local demo placeholders until the Phase 3 signal bus - they are NOT a thermal or CFD result. Human visual sign-off is still outstanding (WP-14). MEASURED WHILE BUILDING: in the Phase 2a machine the part sits INSIDE the induction enclosure shell (shell AABB x -0.825..0.825, y 0.32..1.87, z -1.1..0.2; part AABB x -0.069..0.119, y 1.023..1.177, z -0.227..-0.073) and that shell has no opening at the fixture, so from every camera outside it the part is hidden behind the shell and the 0.45-opacity door glazing - the wp-ref-part capture is byte-identical across versions even when the part was enlarged 3.3x, which is why that pose cannot gate the part. The committed part view (wp-closeup) is a free camera inside the enclosure. If scenarios need to see the part in place, Phase 2a's shell or door needs an opening at the fixture: that changes the accepted induction model and must be reviewed, not slipped in.

items.title: overall silhouette and proportions (bell with stem)
items.note: A bell/bowl shaped outer race with a stem exiting the closed end, read from the part on the induction fixture in PHOTO-05 and the wet stem in PHOTO-09. Height ~0.18 m and bell diameter ~0.15 m in the model are ESTIMATED from photo proportions, not measured; no drawing or CAD exists (NV-011).

items.title: bell / bowl wall with three tripod window openings
items.note: The wall is built as three lathe segments so the three windows are real openings with wall thickness, matching the tripod-style outer race described as CV OR in the sources. Window width, wall thickness and the exact three-window geometry are ESTIMATED - PHOTO-05 is the only close-up and the sheen hides the edges.

items.title: window edge rails and bell mouth lip
items.note: Six vertical rails frame the three openings and a lip ring finishes the open mouth. Both are inference: at the resolution available the wall edge could equally be a plain chamfer. Positions ESTIMATED from PHOTO-05.

items.title: stem / shaft and stem heat zone
items.note: Stem modelled as a tapered shaft exiting the bell base, matching the 'stem quench' station in PHOTO-09 and the Z2 stem axis positions (PR-002, ~22-112.8 mm). Stem diameter and length are ESTIMATED from photo proportions; the axial position range in PR-002 is a machine axis range, not a part dimension, and was not used as one.

items.title: spline drive feature on the stem
items.note: A spline end is modelled only because the documents reference Go/NoGo spline gages and OPD checks (EQ-007); the tooth count (16), tooth form and spline length are pure ASSUMPTION - no source states them and no photograph resolves the stem end clearly.

items.title: clamp journal and fixture interface
items.note: A machined clamp journal is modelled where the Phase 2a fixture jaws grip the part, and the interior seating face supports the QN-002 check (OK = part fully seated and centred, NOK = tilted or off-centre). The journal diameter/length are ESTIMATED; the model has no clamping animation yet.

items.title: interior features: seating face and cage seat ring
items.note: The bell interior is never visible in any source photograph and no drawing exists, so the interior seating face and the cage/roller seat ring are modelled as plain ASSUMED geometry sized to fit the openings. Treat every interior surface as illustrative only.

evidence.sourceId: no photographic coverage of the bell interior; interior geometry assumed

items.title: base flange and mounting holes
items.note: A base flange with six evenly spaced holes is modelled as an ASSUMED mounting / locating pattern. No source shows a flange or a bolt pattern on this part - this is an invention to give the fixture something to clamp and must be verified or removed against a controlled drawing.

evidence.sourceId: no source shows a flange or bolt pattern on the CV OR part

items.title: part marks: 2D DataMatrix code, OPD dot, 'V', numbering 1-5
items.note: The marks themselves are documented - laser DataMatrix marking (EQ-005) read by the 2D camera (EQ-006, EP-002), the bearing-face dot mark (GD-004) and the OK 'V' mark (GS-004) - but their POSITIONS and sizes on the part are assumed placements, and the GD-004 numbering 1-5 is represented by a single stand-in label rather than five number marks.

items.title: machined finish bands and chamfers
items.note: Stem-end and mouth chamfers plus one ground finish band are modelled to break the silhouette edges (PHOTO-09 gloss). Count, width and position are ESTIMATED from the photograph; no surface finish specification is available, so no roughness value is claimed as plant data.

items.title: L5 heat visualisation (bell colour, stem heat band)
items.note: Two L5 overlay meshes follow QN-004 (OK = uniform straw/gray bell, NOK = spot overheating, scale, cracks) and QN-005 (OK = clean heat band on the stem, NOK = discoloration beyond the band). They are driven by the same demo HEAT state as the coil, so the glow is a placeholder, not a thermal result or a validated colour scale; the failure modes are not modelled.

items.title: coolant / oil film (conceptual)
items.note: One translucent conceptual shell stands in for the coolant/oil sheen on the part and fixture area in PHOTO-05. It carries no wetting, flow or drainage behaviour and is the first thing to remove if it is read as a process claim.

items.title: comparison renders committed
items.note: Renders committed in docs/compare/workpiece/: model_v3 (+ _side, _overlay, _metrics.json) is the wp-ref-part photo-match attempt against PHOTO-09 and model_wpc_v3 is the free wp-closeup capture from inside the enclosure. The photo-match attempt does NOT gate the part: the part is hidden behind the enclosure from that camera, so model_v1/v2/v3 are byte-identical (metrics luma 58.5 vs 109.4, edges 1.95 vs 4.52, hist_cos 0.228 - all measuring the machine, not the part). Only model_wpc_v3 shows the workpiece (mean luma 43.7), and it has no reference photograph to compare against (NV-018). Superseded wp-closeup captures taken outside the door glass were deleted rather than kept as false evidence.

items.title: human visual sign-off of the comparison renders
items.note: Outstanding. Renders exist but have not been reviewed by a human, and no photograph isolates the workpiece, so the increment-3 gate cannot be cleared on the strength of the comparison renders alone - a drawing or a dedicated part photograph is needed.
